reports.title: UAE foundational statistical-system meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from FCSC and CBUAE sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding the FCSC institutional core, population, national accounts, CPI, CBUAE institutional role and BOP into the opening foundation layer for UAE research.
reports._notes: Opening integrating node. Hydrocarbon + diversified services/logistics structure will guide subsequent densification.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch

reports.title: OPEC+ / Declaration of Cooperation production-policy framing
reports.publisher: Derived from OPEC and monitoring sources
reports.description: System-level framing of the OPEC+ (Declaration of Cooperation) production-policy architecture. Core members continue to set output adjustments that influence global crude supply and price formation. UAE departure in May 2026 reduced the group’s share of world production and capacity but did not eliminate the mechanism.

reports.title: UAE exit from OPEC (May 2026)
reports.publisher: Derived from official and monitoring sources
reports.description: One-off foundational event: the United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC effective 1 May 2026. The exit reduced OPEC’s and OPEC+’s share of global crude production and capacity; the UAE retains independent production and export policy while remaining a major global supplier.

reports.title: Sovereign wealth funds framing (ADIA, Mubadala)
reports.publisher: Derived from fund and official sources
reports.description: Framing of the major Abu Dhabi sovereign investment vehicles (ADIA, Mubadala and related). Multi-hundred-billion-dollar asset bases; dual role in international portfolio investment and domestic diversification under national strategies.

reports.title: UAE oil–sovereign–labour densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from energy, fund and labour sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding oil production/exports, sovereign wealth fund framing, and labour/expatriate statistics into a coherent hydrocarbon–investment–labour layer.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
National accounts, BOP and CBUAE series from Batch 1

reports.title: Dubai economic and logistics framing
reports.publisher: Derived from FCSC and Dubai monitoring sources
reports.description: Framing of Dubai as the principal non-oil, services, logistics, tourism and finance hub. Dominates container throughput (Jebel Ali), visitor arrivals, trade facilitation and private-sector services activity within the federation.
reports._notes: Primary Dubai densification. Complements the federal non-oil structure.

reports.title: Abu Dhabi economic and hydrocarbon framing
reports.publisher: Derived from FCSC and Abu Dhabi sources
reports.description: Framing of Abu Dhabi as the principal hydrocarbon, sovereign-wealth and capital emirate. Hosts the bulk of oil and gas production, ADNOC, ADIA/Mubadala and the federal capital functions.
reports._notes: Primary Abu Dhabi densification. Complements the federal hydrocarbon core.

reports.title: Ports and container throughput statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from DP World and logistics sources
reports.description: Statistics on container and cargo throughput, centred on Jebel Ali and other UAE ports. The UAE is a major global transshipment and logistics node; throughput is continuously referenced in trade, diversification and regional-hub analysis.
reports._notes: Core logistics densification under global-hub structure.

reports.title: UAE Dubai–Abu Dhabi–logistics–tourism densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from emirate and sector sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding Dubai framing, Abu Dhabi framing, ports/logistics statistics and tourism statistics into a coherent dual-emirate and services-hub layer.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch

reports.title: Abu Dhabi hydrocarbon and sovereign-wealth hub framing

reports.title: GCC Customs Union and Common Market framing
reports.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Finance and GCC sources
reports.description: Framing of the UAE’s membership in the GCC Customs Union and Common Market. Common external tariff, free movement of goods, and ongoing work to complete remaining Customs Union requirements are structural features of the external trade regime.

reports.title: Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth architecture framing (ADIA, Mubadala, related)
reports.publisher: Derived from fund and official sources
reports.description: System-level framing of the major Abu Dhabi sovereign investment vehicles. Multi-hundred-billion-dollar asset bases; dual role in international portfolio investment and domestic diversification.

reports.title: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) sovereign wealth framing
reports.publisher: Derived from ADIA and secondary monitoring sources
reports.description: Framing of ADIA as Abu Dhabi’s traditional long-term sovereign wealth fund. Estimated assets under management in the order of US$1 trillion; invests primarily outside the UAE and is a core vehicle for intergenerational management of hydrocarbon surpluses.

reports.publisher: Derived from national energy and climate sources
reports.description: System-level framing of the UAE’s simultaneous hydrocarbon production role and renewable/energy-transition ambitions. Links oil production, sovereign investment, renewable capacity expansion and climate reporting.

findings.title: Ports and container throughput statistics
findings.finding: Still not found, and the item is partly ineligible: DP World, the source the item is derived from, is a corporate publisher. On the official side, the FCSC statistics index (https://fcsc.gov.ae/en-us/Pages/Statistics/Statistics.aspx) was retrieved and lists Transport 2013-2022 and Transport 2024 but exposes no hyperlinks to them, its UAE.STAT data explorer (uaestat.fcsc.gov.ae) is disallowed by robots.txt, and opendata.fcsc.gov.ae fails its robots.txt fetch. SCAD (scad.gov.ae) is reachable and its Transport & Services theme was retrieved, but the indicators tab returns 'No Indicators Available Yet' and the only products are Excel workbooks (e.g. Transport Statistics-Annually 2024) whose contents could not be read to verify any container/TEU or cargo-throughput table - and they would in any case cover Abu Dhabi only, not Jebel Ali. Dubai Statistics Center (dsc.gov.ae) serves only a login interface. No official UAE container-throughput product could be retrieved and verified.
